thread:
dmitri: CI red on main -> flaky unit: test_session_ttl_expiry keeps failing in CI (only on linux-worker, about 1/20 runs). Anyone seen this recently?

carla: saw one earlier this week but chalked it up to noise. Can you paste the failing log? :eyes:

ci-bot: job failed: build/serve-tests #4521 (linux-x86_64) - failure: test_session_ttl_expiry

ci-bot: link: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/4521

dmitri: logs attached below — the test asserts session still valid after a short sleep. Sometimes the ttl check kicks in ~30ms early.

```
--- FAIL: TestSessionTTLExpiry (0.04s)
    session_test.go:128: expected active session, got expired
    runtime_timer.go:87: timer fired at 2026-03-15T11:23:45.123Z (delta -34ms)
    goroutine 12 [running]:
      github.com/redwood/inference/runtime.(*Session).CheckTTL(...)
```

bob: looks like a timing window. Are we using real time in tests? If so, CI worker load variance could cause early expiration. We should either fake the clock or widen the window.

alice: quick triage plan: 1) rerun the failed job to confirm flakiness 2) try the test with GOMAXPROCS=1 and a mocked clock 3) if repro, bisect for regressing commit. anyone want to take step 1?

jen: rerunning now (build/serve-tests #4521) -> queued. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

carla: for a fast workaround we can bump TestSessionTTLExpiry delta from 50ms to 120ms while we root cause, but prefer to add deterministic clock.

dmitri: +1 on both — open to making change behind a flag to avoid masking real regressions.

bob: for bisect: suspect range is between commit 64a1b2 (timer refactor) and 9d8f7c (scheduler change). I can run a local git bisect tomorrow if rerun repros.

ci-bot: rerun started: build/serve-tests #4521 (retry 1) -> running on linux-12

alice: FYI if someone wants a quick local repro: run `go test ./runtime -run TestSessionTTLExpiry -race -count=50` on linux VM, you'll likely see it within ~50 runs. Use `GOMAXPROCS=2` to increase chance.

jen: rerun finished: flaky — failed again (2/2). CI job output shows the same early timer fire.

dmitri: ok confirmed. bob, can you kick off the bisect on CI? tag me if you hit a noisy commit and I'll help narrow.

bob: starting automated bisect across suspected range. If it narrows, I'll post the culprit. Might take ~30m. :coffee:

alice: small note — don't forget to look at scheduler backoff patch in 9d8f7c, it adjusted timer jitter math which might interact with our TTL rounding.

carla: also add a unit test harness with a fake clock for Session.checkTTL, that should make it deterministic and faster to iterate. I'll add a draft PR.

bob: bisect result: (prelim) commit 8f3c2be introduced a subtle race where timers can be rescheduled with negative delta under high load. marking as likely culprit.

dmitri: nice find. Can we get a minimal repro in a test? If so, we can either fix the reschedule logic or make CheckTTL robust to small negative deltas.

carla: opening PR with two parts: 1) replace real-time use in TestSessionTTLExpiry with fake clock 2) guard CheckTTL to treat deltas within -50ms..+50ms as still valid (log a warning). Draft up in #PR-1247.

alice: assign reviewers: @bob @dmitri. If tests pass in CI with fake clock, we can revert temp timeout bump.

jen: CI for PR-1247 queued. good job team. :tada:

ci-bot: PR-1247 CI: running unit tests (linux)

alice: follow-up: we should add a perf note for timer jitter in the runtime docs so oncall knows this class of flakes and the quick fixes (fake clock, GOMAXPROCS, small delta guards). I'll add a short blurb in eng-runtime/wiki.

dmitri: thanks all — will monitor PR and merge once CI is green.

carla: merged and released patch to main. Monitoring for next 24h. :rocket:
